dva-med-025.text: A function Lambda processes batches of 10 messages from SQS. When UMA message of the batch fails, the whole batch returns to the row and the 9 successful are reprocessed. Which configuration avoids this unnecessary reprocessing?
options: Enable partial batch response (ReportBatchItemFailures) and return in response only the failed message IDs
Increase the lot's visibility timeout
Reduce batch size to 1 message
Capture all exceptions and fake success always
dva-med-025.explanation: With the partial failure report activated in the event source mapping, only the messages listed as failures return to the queue — the others are confirmed, eliminating reprocessing and duplicate effects.
dva-med-025.hint: Teach the function to deliver the 'list of the undefeated' — only they repeat the proof.
optionRationales: With the partial failure report activated in the event source mapping, only the messages listed as failures return to the queue — the others are confirmed, eliminating reprocessing and duplicate effects.
Unit batches resolve the symptom by sacrificing the throughput and multiplying invocations — partial response keeps the batches efficient.
Swallowing bugs confirms error messages — silent data loss.
More invisibility time does not change the semantics of 'the whole lot fails together'.

dva-med-026.text: A topic SNS receives requests events of all kinds, but the 'refunds' row should only receive messages whose 'type' attribute is 'refunds', without the consumer discarding the rest. SNS implements this selection in the signature itself?
options: Filter policies (filter policies) on the signature, delivering only messages whose attributes marry the filter
Make the queue reject messages based on content
Configure the consumer to delete what does not matter
Create a topic for each type of event possible
dva-med-026.explanation: The filter policy evaluates the attributes (or body) of the message in delivery: each subscriber receives only what interests him — eliminating traffic and discard logic in consumers.
dva-med-026.hint: The signature can have a 'attribute carrier': only message that matches the policy enters.
optionRationales: The filter policy evaluates the attributes (or body) of the message in delivery: each subscriber receives only what interests him — eliminating traffic and discard logic in consumers.
Multiplying topics fragments publication and complicates producers — filter resolves signature.
The SQS does not filter content in the input — selection takes place at the signature of the SNS.
Discarding in the consumer waste delivery, processing and cost — the filter prevents the message from even arriving.

dva-med-027.text: A report should be generated automatically every Monday at 7h, invoking a function Lambda. Which service schedules this recurring execution with cron expressions, without servers?
options: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler (or scheduled rules of EventBridge) with cron expression invoking the function
Configure the schedule in the console of S3
An instance EC2 with crontab calling the function
A loop with sleep within its own function Lambda
dva-med-027.explanation: The EventBridge Scheduler shoots targets in fully managed cron/rate calendars — the standard crontab serverless for recurring tasks.
dva-med-027.hint: The 'managed alarm' of AWS speaks cron and invokes targets — no machine turned on.
optionRationales: The EventBridge Scheduler shoots targets in fully managed cron/rate calendars — the standard crontab serverless for recurring tasks.
Functions have limit of 15 minutes and time charge — sleeping inside them is unfeasible and expensive.
Dedicated server to schedule contradicts serverless — managed scheduler eliminates this machine.
The S3 triggers events from OBJETOS — does not have cron task scheduler.

dva-med-028.text: A team evaluates Step Functions for two flows: (A) an approval process that can last days, with complete audit of each step; (B) a pipeline of ingestion of high volume and short duration events (less than 5 minutes) where the cost per execution matters. Which type of workflow best serves each case?
options: Neither.; Step Functions only execute streams of up to 15 minutes
Standard for both, because Express was discontinued
Express for flow A, because approvals require express speed
Standard for flow A (long duration, exact-one-view execution, complete history) and Express for flow B (high volume, short duration, lower usage cost))
dva-med-028.explanation: Workflows Standard support even 1 year with auditable history; Express are optimized for volume and cost in executions up to 5 minutes with semantics by-minus-a-vez — the classic choice per profile.
dva-med-028.hint: Auditory marathon vs. cheap sprint in mass: each type of workflow has its track.
optionRationales: Workflows Standard support even 1 year with auditable history; Express are optimized for volume and cost in executions up to 5 minutes with semantics by-minus-a-vez — the classic choice per profile.
Express is limited to 5 minutes of duration — unfeasible for day processes.
Express follows active and is the recommended option for high volume short duration.
The limit of 15 minutes is from Lambda — Standard workflows last up to one year.

dva-med-029.text: A flow of Step Functions receives an array with variable number of requests and needs to execute the MESMO set of steps for each request, with controlled parallelism. Which state of the machine is designed for this dynamic iteration?
options: The State of Choice evaluating each order
The Wait state among the requests
The Map status, which will go over the array items applying the sub-flow to each, with configurable competition
The Parallel state, creating a branch on request manually
dva-med-029.explanation: Map is the for-each of Step Functions: processing dynamic-sized collections with parallel limit — different from Parallel, which performs branches FIXOS and other.
dva-med-029.hint: The 'for-each' of the status machine: a state that maps the sub-flow over each item of the array.
optionRationales: Map is the for-each of Step Functions: processing dynamic-sized collections with parallel limit — different from Parallel, which performs branches FIXOS and other.
Parallel requires statically defined branches in the template — does not accompany arrays of variable size.
Choice route the flow by conditions — no iter on collections.
Wait just pauses the flow — without any iteration mechanics.

dva-med-030.text: A platform needs to choose between Kinesis Data Streams SQS for event intake. The decisive requirement: multiple independent consumer applications should read the MESMO flow, and should be possible REPROCESSAR events of the last 24 hours when correcting a bug. What service attends and why?
options: Both are equivalent to that requirement.
SQS FIFO, because ordination allows reprocessing
SQS Standard, because messages can be reread at any time after consumption
Kinesis Data Streams: Records are retained in the stream (24h a 365 days) and several consumers read the same flow of independent positions, allowing replay
dva-med-030.explanation: The stream is a durable and re-readable log: consumers maintain their own pointers and can rewind — in the SQS, the message consumed and deleted disappears forever and each message answers one consumer.
dva-med-030.hint: Fila delivers and burns the letter; stream is the recorded tape that several can hear — and rewind.
optionRationales: The stream is a durable and re-readable log: consumers maintain their own pointers and can rewind — in the SQS, the message consumed and deleted disappears forever and each message answers one consumer.
After being consumed and excluded, the message from SQS no longer exists — there is no replay or multiple readers of the same data.
FIFO sorts and deduplicates, but maintains row semantics: consumption removes message — without rereading by multiple applications.
The difference between row × stream is exactly this: re-readable retention with multiple consumers is exclusive to the stream model.

dva-med-031.text: The creation events of objects of a pocket S3 need to shoot various targets with advanced filtering by event metadata (prefix, size, etc.), going beyond the limited destinations of traditional notifications of S3. What a modern approach to AWS recommends?
options: Configure dozens of overlapping notifications in the pocket itself
Enable integration of S3 with the Amazon EventBridge and create rules with event patterns to route multiple targets
Make every application sweep the bucket from time to time
Use replication between regions as a notification mechanism
dva-med-031.explanation: With the EventBridge enabled in the pocket, events gain rich content filtering and dozens of target types (multiple simultaneous rules) — surpassing direct destinations (Lambda/SQS/SNS) of the classic notifications.
dva-med-031.hint: Connect the bucket to the 'barring': rich rules, many targets, without the classic notification ties.
optionRationales: With the EventBridge enabled in the pocket, events gain rich content filtering and dozens of target types (multiple simultaneous rules) — surpassing direct destinations (Lambda/SQS/SNS) of the classic notifications.
Native notifications limit destinations and prohibit overlapping filters for the same event — the bus removes those restrictions.
Polling journal adds latency and listing cost — the pushed event dispenses scans.
CRR copy objects — does not route events for application targets.

dva-med-032.text: In one API REST of the API Gateway, the team wants you to MESMO deployment serve dev and production, with each stage invoking a different alias of function Lambda (dev → alias 'dev'; prod → alias 'prod'). API Gateway parameters integration by stage?
options: Mapping templates by converting the stage name
Create a API fully separated for each environment, always
Use different plans by environment
Internship variables, referenced in integration (ex: ${stageVariables.lambdaAlias}) to point out the correct alias in each stage
dva-med-032.explanation: Stage variables work as environment variables per stage: the same integration definition resolves different destinations according to the stage — eliminating double configuration.
dva-med-032.hint: Each 'palco' has its own variables — and integration reads them to choose the show alias.
optionRationales: Stage variables work as environment variables per stage: the same integration definition resolves different destinations according to the stage — eliminating double configuration.
Duplicate APIs multiply maintenance — stage variables resolve parameterization in the same API (separate APIs is valid option, but not the requested resource).
Templates transform payloads — do not parameterize the ENDPOINT integration by stage.
Use plans deal with quotas per consumer — do not route integrations for different aliases.

dva-med-033.text: A flow of Step Functions Needs PAUSAR until a human approves the step in an external system, which may take hours — without keeping any function running during the wait. Step Functions implements this waiting by external confirmation?
options: A function Lambda in loop checking approval every second
Callback with task token (.waitForTaskToken): the stream delivers a token to the external system and is paused until it receives SendTaskSuccess/SendTaskFailure with this token
Close the flow and create another manually after approval
A Wait state of fixed duration of 24 hours
dva-med-033.explanation: The callback pattern suspends execution without consuming computer: the token travels to the approval system and the response (success/failure) resumes the flow — ideal for human integrations and slow external systems.
dva-med-033.hint: The stream delivers a 'return sign' and sleeps for free — only wakes up when someone returns the password with the verdict.
optionRationales: The callback pattern suspends execution without consuming computer: the token travels to the approval system and the response (success/failure) resumes the flow — ideal for human integrations and slow external systems.
Polling in function pays duration and bars at the limit of 15 minutes — the opposite of passive callback waiting.
Fixed wait does not react to approval: slows down fast flows and bursts in slow — the callback resumes exactly when the answer arrives.
Breaking the execution loses the state and track of the process — the token keeps everything in a single auditable execution.

dva-med-034.text: A function Lambda ML processing needs libraries and models that add up 4 GB — well beyond the limit of 250 MB of package ZIP. What is the packaging option of the Lambda enable this function?
options: Divide the ZIP in 16 layers of 250 MB
Request an increase in the limit of ZIP Supported
Compress libraries with ZIP double
Pack function as container image (up to 10 GB) published no ECR
dva-med-034.explanation: The Lambda supports up to container images 10 GB: Customized heavy dependencies, models and runtimes enter the image, keeping the serverless execution model.
dva-med-034.hint: When the ZIP does not fit, the function turns 'ship container': until 10 GB via image log.
optionRationales: The Lambda supports up to container images 10 GB: Customized heavy dependencies, models and runtimes enter the image, keeping the serverless execution model.
The limit of 250 MB decompressed goes to the CONJUNTO function+layers — multiply layers does not contour it.
The limit considers the size decompressed — nested compression does not deceive the platform.
The package limit ZIP is not adjustable by ticket — the official way to large artifacts is the image of container.

dva-med-035.text: When running the application locally, the SDK of AWS find credentials without any explicit configuration in the code. What is the general order of the string of credentials providers that SDKs follow?
options: Explicit parameters in the code → environment variables → credentials/profile file → container/roll credentials of the instance (IMDS)
The SDK generates new keys in the first execution
The SDK ask the user's password on the terminal
Only environment variables are supported
dva-med-035.explanation: The credential provider chain searches in order: explicit configuration, env vars (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID...), profiles of ~/.aws, and finally the credentials of the execution environment (ECS/EC2 roll) — so it 'works without setting' on machines with profile or in instances with roll.
dva-med-035.hint: The SDK search for the key in successive pockets: code, environment, profile file and finally the machine roll.
optionRationales: The credential provider chain searches in order: explicit configuration, env vars (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID...), profiles of ~/.aws, and finally the credentials of the execution environment (ECS/EC2 roll) — so it 'works without setting' on machines with profile or in instances with roll.
SDKs do not make interactive prompts — resolution is automatic by the provider chain.
SDKs never create credentials — only locate and use them.
Env vars are just a link in the chain — environmental profiles and roles also participate.

dva-med-036.text: A chat application needs persistent two-way communication: the server should EMPURRAR messages to customers connected in real time, without polling. What kind of API of the Amazon API Gateway supports this model?
options: HTTP API with cache enabled
REST API with aggressive customer polling
WebSocket API, maintaining persistent connections with routes like $connect, $disconnect and custom actions
API Gateway does not support real time; a dedicated server is needed
dva-med-036.explanation: A WebSocket API of the API Gateway manages long-term two-way connections: the backend sends messages to customers via connection IDs — the real-time chat, game and dashboard model.
dva-med-036.hint: For the server 'link' to the client at any time, the API need double hand protocol.
optionRationales: A WebSocket API of the API Gateway manages long-term two-way connections: the backend sends messages to customers via connection IDs — the real-time chat, game and dashboard model.
Polling consumes requests and adds latency — it is not true push nor persistent connection.
Cache accelerates answers REPETIDAS — does not create persistent bidirectional channel.
WebSocket support is native to API Gateway — Dispenses own connection servers.
